title: BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT
body_text:
Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society is officially launched in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.
The implementation of Bharat Taxi Services is being carried out in a phased manner across the country. The implementation includes registration and onboarding of Sarathis (drivers), customer enrolment, training programmes and expansion of services to identified cities and States. As on 04.08.2026, the platform has registered 8.48 lakh Sarathis (drivers) and 44.27 lakh customers. The platform is facilitating 11,106 daily rides and has enabled cumulative earnings of ₹83.70 crore for Sarathis.
The rollout of services of Bharat Taxi, operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), in other cities and States is subject to operational requirements and necessary approvals. Expansion is undertaken based on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions, and other stakeholders.
The details of operation of Bharat Taxi in various cities and average daily rides, as on 04.08.2026, are as under:
City Average Daily rides Delhi- NCR 5574 Gujarat 3817 Lucknow 324 Chandigarh 190 Mumbai 197 Jaipur 372 Pune 632 Total 11,106 .
Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi are separate mobility platforms operating under different institutional frameworks. Bharat Taxi is a cooperative-based mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, whereas Yatri Sathi is a mobility platform developed and operated by the Department of Information Technology and Electronics (DITE), Government of West Bengal.
On 19th July, 2026, STCL entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of West Bengal for collaboration with the Yatri Sathi platform. Under the MoU, Bharat Taxi extends support in the areas of driver enrolment, cooperative membership, driver welfare and public outreach.
This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

enrichment.summary: Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led app-based mobility platform run by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, has been officially rolled out in Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan, with phased expansion to other cities like Lucknow, Chandigarh, Jaipur and Pune. As of 4 August 2026, it has 8.48 lakh registered drivers (Sarathis), 44.27 lakh customers, facilitates 11,106 daily rides, and has generated ₹83.70 crore in cumulative driver earnings. STCL has also signed an MoU with the West Bengal government to support its Yatri Sathi platform through driver enrolment, cooperative membership and welfare initiatives. This information was shared by Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha.
enrichment.context:
Bharat Taxi is part of the government's broader push to strengthen the cooperative sector as an alternative economic model to private, profit-driven platforms in the gig economy, particularly ride-hailing services dominated by companies like Ola and Uber. The Ministry of Cooperation, created in 2021 with the vision of 'Sahakar se Samriddhi' (prosperity through cooperation), has been promoting multistate cooperative societies in sectors like organic products (Bharat Organics), exports (Sahakar Bharat Exports), and now urban mobility, aiming to ensure better earnings and welfare for gig workers like taxi drivers by giving them ownership stakes rather than treating them purely as platform labour.

The distinction drawn between Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi is significant: while Bharat Taxi operates under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 as a cooperative enterprise, Yatri Sathi is a state government-run digital platform in West Bengal. Their collaboration via an MoU reflects an emerging model of cooperative federalism, where a national cooperative body supports state-run digital initiatives in areas like driver welfare and outreach without merging operations, illustrating how centrally promoted cooperative platforms can complement rather than compete with state government digital public infrastructure.

prelims_questions.question: Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led mobility platform recently launched in India, is operated under which of the following legal frameworks?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that Bharat Taxi is operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi is correct?
options: Both are operated by the same central government ministry
Yatri Sathi is a cooperative platform while Bharat Taxi is run by the West Bengal government
Bharat Taxi is a cooperative platform under STCL, while Yatri Sathi is run by the Government of West Bengal's IT department
Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi have merged into a single platform
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, Bharat Taxi is operated by STCL under the Ministry of Cooperation's cooperative framework, while Yatri Sathi is developed and operated by the Department of Information Technology and Electronics, Government of West Bengal; the two remain separate but have signed an MoU for collaboration.
